rationale: Record the drift-then-trim receipt and move the child question to violated. With every node's recorded accepted index inflated (node 1: 10, node 2: 9, node 3: 7, all over six indices of content), the public trim(None) on the leader returned no error and compacted index 7 - past the leader's own six indices of content and past the index its five entries occupy - and the leader's reads of indices 5 and 6 then reported trimmed with a two-element decided-log read, while the declared comparison requiring the compacted index to reach the six indices the configuration decided was violated (witness index 12). A behaviour records that trim accepts a drifted bound and compacts past the content, and the child interpretation states the finding with its basis, the counterevidence that the documented precondition is only satisfiable in the drifted bookkeeping (every node's decided report also drifted), and the limits that the over-compaction's downstream hazard (suffix requests below the compacted index underflowing in MemoryStorage) was not triggered and that the baseline comparisons of this run are unknown because they were admitted through an event name shared with another case.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a suffix or log-sync request below the compacted index occurs after an over-compaction (for example from a replica whose recorded accepted index is still truthful or from a freshly started instance), which MemoryStorage would evaluate as a subtraction below its compacted index; the decisive observation is a panic or a silently empty suffix on that path.

knowledge.statement: trim on a leader whose recorded accepted indexes have drifted accepts a bound above the entries the configuration holds: with every recorded value above the content, trim(None) took the minimum recorded accepted index, found it inside the drifted decided index, and compacted that many indices, leaving the compacted index above the entries the leader held and the reads of the trimmed region reporting Trimmed.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, three reconnection rounds and a leader change, so that the minimum recorded accepted index (7) exceeded the content (5 entries plus a StopSign) while the Drifted decided index (9) covered it; observed in receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a: trim_outcome ok, compacted index 7, leader accepted 9 and decided 9 (event 12), reads of indices 5 and 6 reported trimmed afterwards with a two-element decided-log read (event 14), and the followers' recorded values stayed at 10 and 7 with decided 9 (events 13, 15). Sourced by the trim derivation and the minimum helper; the drift is the parent question's witnessed consequence.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed: the drifted accepted indexes reach the trim bound, and trim acts on it. Receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a: after three reconnection rounds and a leader change, the leader held six indices of content (five entries plus the StopSign) while the recorded accepted indexes were 10, 9 and 7 and every node's decided report had drifted to 9 (events 9-11); the public trim(None) then returned no error and compacted index 7 (event 12), i.e. more indices than the log contains and more than the five entry indices, and the leader's subsequent reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed with a two-element decided-log read (event 14) while both followers still reported accepted 10 and 7 with decided 9 (events 13, 15). The declared comparison requiring the compacted index to reach the six decided indices was violated at that event, and the comparison requiring trim to succeed was recorded unknown only because its admission chain was built on an event name shared with another case in the same execution; the sampled operands show the call returned Ok. The mechanism is the child question's premise: trim derives its bound from the minimum recorded accepted index (util.rs 186-191) and compares it against the leader's decided index (mod.rs 141-170) rather than against what each replica holds, so once the drift lifts those recorded values the leader's own content no longer bounds the compaction. The documented requirement that all nodes have decided the trim index is met only in the same drifted bookkeeping (their decided reports are drifted too), which is why I keep the counterevidence explicit rather than treating the documentation as the violated duty; the duty that fails on admissible input is that the trim bound must not exceed the entries the leader itself holds, and it does here.
counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented precondition (all nodes decided the trim index) was satisfied in the drifted bookkeeping; the violated obligation I rely on is instead that the compacted index must stay within the content the leader holds, which it did not (7 against 6 indices).
The trim call itself returned Ok, so nothing in the call's own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.
limitations: The downstream hazard I sourced (a later suffix request below the compacted index underflowing MemoryStorage's arithmetic) was not triggered: no promise or log-sync in this run asked for a prefix below the compacted index, so the over-compaction is witnessed with reads and the compacted index, not with a crash.

The baseline comparisons of this receipt are unknown because they were admitted through an event name shared with another case in the same execution; the pre-trim state is asserted from the sampled operands (events 9-11).
The drift and therefore the over-compaction were produced with three reconnection rounds and one leader change in a three-node cluster; other sizes, rounds and producers were not exercised.
No snapshot was created, so after the trim the entries were simply removed; whether a snapshot-enabled configuration would instead compact into a snapshot that no replica can serve was not exercised.
